words.name: QUANTIZE
words.summary: Puts x at a width and scale exponent; how a non-integer enters a program.
words.documentation:
QUANTIZE — Puts x at a width and scale exponent; how a non-integer enters a program.
Syntax: x width exponent QUANTIZE
Width: The width named: 8, 16, 32 or 64.
Scale: The exponent named, within ±31.
Error: Raising the exponent rounds half to even, adding at most half an ulp of the new scale; lowering it is exact. A literal p/q is rounded once, where it is written.
field: Leaving (mayOverflow) when the value may not fit the width: it is then 1/0. Writing 1/0 or 0/0 is leaving (wheelPoint).
Example: 1/3 8 -6 QUANTIZE  →  21/64

words.name: ADD
words.summary: The exact sum, lane by lane.
words.documentation:
ADD — The exact sum, lane by lane.
Syntax: a b ADD
Width: Widened to the narrowest width that holds the sum of the operands' ranges; int64 at most.
Scale: The smaller of the two exponents: the other operand is shifted to it exactly.
Error: Exact: the result's budget is the sum of the operands' budgets.
field: Leaving when the sum may leave int64 (mayOverflow) or an operand is a wheel point.
Example: 126 1 ADD  →  127/1

words.name: SUB
words.summary: The exact difference a − b, lane by lane.
words.documentation:
SUB — The exact difference a − b, lane by lane.
Syntax: a b SUB
Width: As ADD: the narrowest width holding the difference of the ranges.
Scale: The smaller of the two exponents.
Error: Exact: the budgets add.
field: As ADD.
Example: 7 3 SUB  →  4/1

words.name: MUL
words.summary: The exact product, lane by lane.
words.documentation:
MUL — The exact product, lane by lane.
Syntax: a b MUL
Width: Widened to the narrowest width holding the product of the ranges: int8 × int8 is int16.
Scale: The sum of the two exponents; an exponent beyond ±31 is an ERROR.
Error: Exact: each operand's budget is scaled by the other's range, as the product propagates it.
field: Leaving when the product may leave int64 or an operand is a wheel point.
Example: 100 100 MUL  →  10000/1

words.name: DIV
words.summary: The quotient a / b, rounded: one of Arare's three rounding points.
words.documentation:
DIV — The quotient a / b, rounded: one of Arare's three rounding points.
Syntax: a b DIV
Width: The narrowest width holding the dividend's range shifted by the divisor's exponent.
Scale: The dividend's exponent: write the dividend at a finer scale for a finer quotient.
Error: Rounds half to even: adds at most half an ulp of the result's scale.
field: Leaving (divisorMayBeZero) when the divisor may be 0: x/0 is 1/0 and 0/0 is ⊥.
Example: 7 2 DIV  →  4/1

words.name: RESCALE
words.summary: Raises x's exponent by s bits (0 to 62), rounding: one of the three rounding points.
words.documentation:
RESCALE — Raises x's exponent by s bits (0 to 62), rounding: one of the three rounding points.

words.name: EQ
words.summary: Whether two values denote the same, whatever their widths and scales; always TRUE or FALSE.
